items.section: 造り・冷菜 / Sashimi & cold dishes
items.note: Raw salmon, sliced. Comes with soy sauce on the side — Japanese soy sauce is wheat-based, so ask for it left off if that matters.

items.en: Chopped raw tuna 'yukhoe' with a raw egg yolk
items.section: 造り・冷菜 / Sashimi & cold dishes
items.note: Korean-style: diced raw tuna in a sesame-soy dressing with a yolk on top and shredded nori. Stir it together before eating.
The shop's headline fried dish — a local YouTube review is literally titled after it. Wheat-flour dredge.
The default izakaya order. Marinated in soy and ginger, dredged in wheat flour or potato starch, fried to order.
Tiny whole squid, eaten head and all — briny and slightly bitter inside. A spring speciality that this shop keeps on.
本 (hon) is the counter for long thin things — here it means 2 wings.
Finger-length whole fish, eaten bones and all with a squeeze of lemon.
Wheat wrapper, deep fried.
Cheap Showa-era pub food: a thick slice of ham in panko. コ/個 (ko) is the counter for pieces.
Panko crumb plus a wheat-and-fruit brown sauce — doubly not gluten-free.

1 skewer ¥200, 2 skewers ¥350. ぼんじり is the small fatty nub above the tail — rich and juicy, a connoisseur's cut. 串 (kushi) = skewer, so 1串/2串 is how many. Ask for 塩 (shio, salt) rather than タレ (tare) — tare is a wheat-soy glaze.

items.en: Chicken tenderloin wrapped with shiso leaf
items.note: 1 skewer ¥180, 2 skewers ¥300. ささみ is the lean breast fillet; shiso (perilla) gives it a minty-basil lift. Usually salt-grilled, but confirm no soy glaze.
Charcoal-grilled frankfurter. Sausage casings and fillers routinely contain wheat.

A Kyoto speciality — the silky film lifted off simmering soy milk, eaten cold with a dab of soy and wasabi. The soy skin itself is fine; the dipping sauce is the wheat risk, and it may be dashi-based rather than plain soy.
Whole garlic cloves cured in a red-shiso pickle — sharp, sweet-sour, a drinking snack. Pickling liquid often contains soy sauce or bonito extract.
Yes, whale — still an old-school izakaya staple in Japan. Dark, dense, beef-like meat simmered in soy and ginger. Worth knowing what you are ordering.

items.en: Pacific saury simmered with sansho pepper
items.note: Oily autumn fish cooked down in soy until the bones are soft; sansho gives a citrusy, tongue-tingling numbness.

items.en: Fermented soybeans with grated mountain yam
items.note: Two famously slimy things at once. Natto is pungent and stringy, tororo is a slippery grated yam. The sachet dressing usually contains both wheat soy sauce and bonito dashi.
Cold pink duck breast fanned over leaves. The dressing is the gluten question.

items.ja: 釜あげしらすとキューリの酢のもの
items.romaji: kamaage shirasu to kyuuri no sunomono
items.en: Boiled baby whitebait and cucumber in sweet vinegar
items.note: 酢の物 (sunomono) is the palate-cleanser course — cold, sharp, refreshing. しらす are tiny translucent whole fish.

items.ja: みつ葉ともやしのおひたし
items.en: Blanched mitsuba herb and bean sprouts in dashi
items.note: おひたし = greens briefly blanched then steeped in seasoned stock. Mitsuba tastes like a cross between parsley and celery. The steeping liquid is bonito dashi plus soy — so not vegan and not gluten-free by default.
Charred whole until collapsing, skin slipped off, served with ginger and soy. Almost always finished with bonito flakes.
A sac of tiny salted roe, spicy and intensely savoury — eaten in small bites with rice or drink. The curing liquid usually contains soy and sometimes wheat.
A Kansai variety so tender and juicy it is eaten raw, torn by hand. Usually served with a soy or dashi dip.
A block of firm tofu fried so the outside is golden and chewy, then grilled and topped with ginger and spring onion. Plant-based in itself — the poured-over sauce and bonito flakes are what break it.

kyr_nibodamashii_ramen_gion_.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Read from a full-resolution photograph of the in-store menu sheet.

items.note: The whole shop is this bowl. Broth built on dried baby sardines with heads and guts left in, so it keeps a real bitter edge — oceanic and savoury, the taste niboshi fans chase and everyone else finds strange. A whole dried sardine sits on top as a garnish. The shop romanises its name NIBO-TAMA on the menu.

items.en: Deluxe niboshi ramen — same bowl plus 3 sheets of nori and a marinated egg
items.note: 特製 (tokusei, 'special') on almost any Japanese ramen menu means the loaded version. Here the extra ¥300 buys exactly 3 sheets of nori and one ajitama.

items.en: Brothless niboshi noodles — noodles tossed in seasoned oil and tare
items.note: 油そば (abura-soba) arrives with no soup: a pool of flavoured oil and tare at the bottom of the bowl. Mix hard from the bottom before the first bite. The table vinegar and chilli are meant for it.
大盛り (oomori) = extra noodles. Here it costs nothing, so say 大盛りで (oomori de) when you order if you are hungry. 並 (nami) would be the regular size.
Also written 味玉 (ajitama) at most shops — a jammy-yolked egg steeped in soy tare. The single most-ordered ramen topping in Japan.
Dip a sheet into the broth to soften, then wrap a mouthful of noodles in it.
A heap of raw sliced green onion — cuts through the oil of a niboshi bowl.
Ferociously sour and salty. Unusual on ramen — it works with the sardine broth. Some are cured with bonito or soy.
Japanese-market kimchi commonly contains fish sauce or salted shrimp, and the seasoning can carry wheat.
The braised pork belly or loin slices. On most menus the pre-loaded version is called チャーシュー麺.
Melts into the oil of the abura-soba rather than the ramen — that is how regulars use it.

items.en: Rare-cooked pork over rice, small bowl
items.note: 生 here means the pork is cooked low and slow so it stays pink and soft, laid over rice with a yolk. A ¥500 mini bowl, not a full meal.

items.en: Rice topped with dried sardine, nori and chilli
items.note: いりこ is the western-Japan word for the same dried sardines the broth is made from. The house move: eat half, then tip the rest into the leftover ramen broth.
卵かけご飯 abbreviated. Crack the raw egg on hot rice, add the soy tare, stir until glossy. A national comfort food — eggs are safe to eat raw in Japan. The tare is wheat soy.
Barley-based, so not gluten-free.
中瓶 is the standard 500ml izakaya bottle. Price not legible on the menu photo.

items.ja: ソフトドリンク（ウーロン茶・緑茶・ジャスミン茶・紅茶）
items.en: Soft drinks — oolong tea, green tea, jasmine tea, black tea
items.note: Price not legible on the menu photo.

items.ja: 卓上調味料（一味タレ・黒胡椒・ホワイトペッパー・煮干し酢）
items.en: On-table seasonings: chilli tare, black pepper, white pepper, niboshi vinegar
items.note: The 煮干し酢 (sardine vinegar) is the unusual one — a splash sharpens the bitterness partway through. The chilli tare is soy-based.

kyr_chuka_rokuroku.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. From the shop's printed menu book and its current handwritten lunch board, photographed August 2026. A 2023 board circulating online is ¥140 lower on the tantanmen — do not use it.

items.section: お昼のお品書き / Lunch board
items.note: 定食 = a main plus rice, soup and a side, priced as one. Changes weekly (a recent one was pork and wood-ear with egg). ¥1,300 with the almond jelly dessert added.

items.en: Dan dan noodles set, with rice or almond jelly
items.section: お昼のお品書き / Lunch board
items.note: ¥1,000 for the bowl alone. This shop's version is famously sour as well as numbing-hot — heavy on minced pork, pak choi and Sichuan pepper. Ask for it 汁なし (shirunashi, brothless) if you prefer.

items.ja: チャーシューと葱の広東風あえ麺Set
items.romaji: chaashuu to negi no kanton-fuu aemen setto
items.en: Cantonese-style tossed noodles with roast pork and spring onion, set
items.section: お昼のお品書き / Lunch board
items.note: あえ麺 (aemen) = no soup, noodles tossed in sauce and oil. ¥1,100 as a single dish.

items.ja: チャーハン（スープ・杏仁豆腐付）
items.en: Fried rice, with soup and almond jelly
items.section: お昼のお品書き / Lunch board
items.note: チャーハン and 焼めし mean the same thing — wok-fried rice with egg and pork. Seasoned with soy, so wheat.

items.ja: 魯肉飯（スープ・杏仁豆腐付）
items.en: Taiwanese braised pork over rice, with soup and almond jelly
items.section: お昼のお品書き / Lunch board
items.note: Lu rou fan — finely chopped fatty pork slow-braised in soy, five-spice and rice wine, ladled over rice. Sweet, sticky, deeply savoury.

items.en: Crisp-fried noodles under a thick five-ingredient gravy, set
items.section: お昼のお品書き / Lunch board
items.note: 五目 (gomoku) = 'five things', i.e. mixed. あんかけ = a starch-thickened glossy sauce poured over. ¥1,400 as a single dish. The noodles go from crunchy to soft as you eat.

items.ja: 細切り豚肉とザーサイのあんかけ汁そば
items.romaji: hosogiri butaniku to zaasai no ankake shiru-soba
items.en: Noodle soup with shredded pork and pickled mustard stem in thick gravy
items.section: お昼のお品書き / Lunch board
items.note: ザーサイ (zha cai) is a crunchy salty Sichuan pickle. ¥1,200 without the rice or dessert.

items.section: お昼のお品書き / Lunch board
items.note: 冷やし = served cold, a summer-only listing. ¥1,200 alone.

items.en: Cold Chinese-style noodle salad with mixed toppings, set
items.section: お昼のお品書き / Lunch board
items.note: 冷やし中華 is the Japanese summer classic: chilled noodles fanned with ham, egg strips, cucumber and a tart soy-vinegar dressing. ¥1,400 alone.
Silky-skinned wontons floating alongside the noodles.

items.en: Noodle soup buried under shredded spring onion
items.note: そば on a Chinese menu means wheat ramen noodles, not buckwheat. A mound of raw shredded negi on top.
からし is hot Japanese mustard — sinus-clearing rather than chilli-hot. A Kyoto-specific noodle genre.
The Kansai word for chahan. Same dish.
Genuinely gluten-free and vegan as long as it is plain — not fried, not seasoned. The safest thing on the menu.

items.en: Pan-fried pork dumplings with a lacy crisp 'wing', 5 pieces
items.note: 羽根 = the wing: a starch slurry poured into the pan sets into a crisp golden web joining the dumplings. Snap it apart at the table.
水 = water, i.e. boiled rather than fried. Thicker, chewier skins than the pan-fried version.
Open-topped steamed dumplings with a chilli-oil kick. A shop signature.

Lo bak go — grated daikon set with rice flour and dried shrimp or sausage, then sliced and fried until the outside crusts. Rice-flour based but usually contains wheat starch and is fried on a shared surface.
パリパリ is the onomatopoeia for a thin, brittle crunch.
Soy-marinated, flour-dredged, twice-fried.

items.en: Fried chicken under a sweet-sour spring-onion soy dressing
items.note: You lin ji — crisp chicken doused at the last second in a vinegared soy-and-negi sauce, so the skin is half crisp, half soaked.

items.en: Mapo tofu — soft tofu and minced pork in a numbing chilli bean sauce
items.note: The numbness is Sichuan pepper (花椒), separate from the chilli heat. Fermented broad-bean paste and soy both carry wheat, and there is pork mince in it.

items.ja: 大徳寺 小川豆腐さんのプレミアム麻婆
items.en: Premium mapo tofu made with tofu from Ogawa Tofu of Daitoku-ji
items.note: The upgrade uses tofu from a named local maker beside Daitoku-ji temple, a few minutes from the shop. Worth the ¥100 if you like tofu.
Crunchy, salty, chilli-flecked pickle — the cheapest thing to put on the table with a beer. Usually dressed with sesame oil, sometimes soy.
Not tofu despite the name — a soft milk-and-apricot-kernel jelly, the standard Chinese-restaurant dessert. Contains dairy and usually gelatin.
